text.p: Gainsco Inc said it is interested in making an insurance acquisition and expects to hire advisers by the end of the month to help it consider its alternatives.
Gainsco chief executive Joseph Macchia told Reuters that the company would consider opportunities in the excess and surplus lines business as well as in the life and property-casualty businesses.
Although Gainsco is an excess- and surplus-lines insurer, Macchia said the company was willing to expand into other lines of business.
Macchia said he might be interested in a distressed situation in which Gainsco would have an opportunity to turn the company around.
An excess- and surplus-lines insurer provides specialized property or liability coverages when it is unavailable from other insurers.
Gainsco focuses on niche markets such as commercial auto, auto garage, general liability and commercial property.
Gainsco is one of a number of insurers currently considering its strategy amid a rapid consolidation in the U.S. insurance industry.

Many companies are seeking to boost their returns on capital and their competitive positions through a merger or acquisition, according to speakers at the Second Annual Congress on Mergers, Acquisitions and Financings on Thursday and Friday.
In the current environment, insurers face the prospect of either being consolidated or becoming the consolidator, the speakers said.
"Consolidation of our industry is not an option but an absolute necessity," Conseco Inc chief executive Stephen Hilbert told the conference on Thursday.

Even the property-casualty industry, where merger activity has been slow in comparison to the life insurance business, is ripe for an increase in consolidation, said Eric Simpson, a vice president in the property-casualty division of insurance rating agency A.M. Best.
"Some of the pressure points are starting to take hold," Simpson told the conference on Thursday.
"The only way for laggards to play catch up is through a marriage," he said.
The conference was sponsored by Business Strategy Network; Tillinghast-Towers Perrin; Weil, Gotshal & Manges; and A.M. Best Co.
